# Conversion tracking: website Stripe payments ONLY (proposal)

**Owner rule (2026-11-19):** Google Ads and Microsoft Ads count **only Stripe payments generated by
the agile-agilist.com checkout**. Eventbrite and Corsizio are **never** ad conversions; they are
kept as internal data only (the agent still records them, labelled by source).

Per your rules, I changed nothing on WordPress. Section 2 is for your web team; section 3 is
what you click in the ad platforms. Section 5 is how the agent proves the rule holds, every day.

## 1. What I found (read-only checks, 2026-11-19)
| Finding | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Website payments run through **Stripe** (custom register flow, then `/registration-confirmed/`). | You control the whole path. |
| **Corsizio is Stripe-based too**, and invoices or payment links can land in the same Stripe account. | "Stripe payment" ≠ "website payment". The website's payments must be **marked** so they can be told apart. |
| GTM4WP container `GTM-K9627QZB` is configured but **output is OFF**. The container in your handover, `GTM-KNLG4JL5`, isn't injected by any active snippet I could see. | It's unclear which tag container, if any, loads today. Verify first (2.1). |
| The confirmation page reads **`?name=…&course=…` from the URL** and fires on page load. | A tag firing there leaks the buyer's name to the ad platforms. Anyone, including an Eventbrite or Corsizio buyer redirected there, can trigger it without a website payment. |
| Active snippet **"AA — Checkout telemetry"** (9 Nov). I couldn't read it. | Check it before adding tags, so nothing double-fires. |

## 2. Proposed site changes (for your web team)
**2.1 Load exactly one GTM container site-wide.** Choose `GTM-K9627QZB` or `GTM-KNLG4JL5` and
retire the other. Verify with Google Tag Assistant.

**2.2 Mark every website checkout payment.** When the site creates the Stripe Checkout Session /
PaymentIntent, set `metadata.origin = "agile-agilist.com"`, plus `metadata.course` (and
`metadata.seats` if more than 1). This one marker is what makes "website-only" provable. The
agent's Stripe reader counts a payment as *website* only with this marker, or when its Checkout
Session returns to agile-agilist.com. Anything else is labelled Corsizio / other / unknown, and
**never** counted for ads.

**2.3 No personal data in the URL.** Set `success_url` to
`/registration-confirmed/?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}`. `[aa_reg_confirmation]` then looks up
the payment server-side and renders the name and course from Stripe, not from the URL.

**2.4 Fire the purchase event ONLY for a verified website payment, once.** Server-side, retrieve
the session and require **all** of: `payment_status = paid`, `metadata.origin = agile-agilist.com`,
and not already tracked. Only then output:
```js
dataLayer.push({ ecommerce: null });
dataLayer.push({
  event: 'purchase',
  ecommerce: {
    transaction_id: 'cs_…',     // Stripe session id: de-duplicates
    value: 1865.75,             // amount actually paid (after the Black Friday 15%)
    currency: 'USD',
    items: [{ item_name: 'AI-Native Value Architect', item_category: 'AI_NATIVE' }]
  }
});
```
Then mark the session tracked. **No `purchase` event** for a page load without a valid website
session: that covers Eventbrite or Corsizio buyers sent to the page, reloads, and people opening
the URL directly.

**2.5 Remove the old click/registration tags** from GTM: the outbound-click trigger to
`eventbrite.*` ("Eventbrite Click - Register") and any Corsizio conversion tag.

**2.6 Keep the Microsoft Ads tracking suffixes exactly as they are** (your rule).

**2.7 (Later, optional)** On landing, store `gclid` / `wbraid` / `msclkid` in a first-party cookie
and copy them into the Stripe payment metadata. That enables server-side conversion uploads, which
survive ad blockers.

## 3. Ad-platform setup (you, in the UIs)
**Google Ads** → Goals → Conversions:
- **New** → Website → *Add manually*: name **`Website Purchase - Paid Registration`** (exactly:
  the agent matches this name), category **Purchase**, value *use different values*, count
  **One**, click-through window 30 days.
- GTM: **Conversion Linker** (all pages) + **Google Ads Conversion Tracking** on custom event
  `purchase`, with value, currency and transaction ID from the data layer.
- **Eventbrite Click - Register** and **Corsizio Registration - AI-Native** (`AW-17013571967/…`):
  set to **secondary** (keeps their history out of bidding and out of the Conversions column), or
  remove them.

**Microsoft Ads** (UET 343248805) → Conversion goals:
- **New** → Event, action `purchase`, revenue dynamic, count **Unique**, name
  `Website Purchase - Paid Registration`; UET event tag on `purchase` in GTM.
- **Eventbrite Click - Register** goal → untick *Include in "Conversions"* (or pause it).

## 4. Cut-over order: do it in one go, after the tag is verified
1. Web team ships 2.1-2.5. Verify with section 5, steps 1-3.
2. **The same day:** make `Website Purchase - Paid Registration` the **primary** goal and demote
   Eventbrite / Corsizio. Don't demote first: campaigns on Maximize Conversions with no valid
   primary goal bid blind.
3. **Bid strategy (your approval needed):** your constitution blocks smart bidding until a
   campaign has **≥15 verified registrations in 30 days**. Website purchases will start near zero,
   so move **Maximize Conversions** campaigns to **Maximize Clicks with a CPC cap** at cut-over,
   then move back campaign by campaign once each passes 15 website purchases in 30 days. This is
   the first time that number will be real, which is the path to Phase 2.
4. If cut-over lands during Black Friday, still do it: optimizing toward Eventbrite clicks you've
   ruled out is worse than a brief adjustment. The promotion assets keep running regardless.

## 5. How the agent proves "website Stripe only", daily
The updated Google Ads Script logs, per campaign: primary conversions, **website purchases**, and
**primary conversions from any other action**. The daily run then alerts you if:
- **any non-website action counts as primary** (e.g. Eventbrite clicks still on) → names the campaigns;
- **Google reports more website purchases than Stripe recorded website payments** (3-day window)
  → the tag is double-firing or counting non-website payments;
- **a Stripe payment has no website marker** → it's held as "origin unknown" and not counted, and
  you're told to fix the marker.

Verification steps:
1. Stripe **test-mode** website purchase → GTM Preview shows **one** `purchase` with the right value.
2. Open `/registration-confirmed/` **without** a session, and reload after a purchase → **no** event.
3. Tag Assistant / UET Tag Helper → tags fire, and **no name or email appears in any URL**.
4. After live sales: the agent's daily email shows website payments vs Google's count, and they
   reconcile. If Google ever shows more, the alert fires.
